Reference guide

Glossary and notation

Author-reviewed

Find a definition, check a symbol, then return to its full argument.

Definitions here are concise. The linked chapter supplies the model, assumptions, proofs and source context. A symbol can mean different things in different chapters; the local definition always controls.

Definitions · Notation and units

Definitions

Accrual

Revenue or expense recognized when the underlying economic event occurs under the stated accounting policy, which can differ from cash receipt or payment.

A profitable period need not generate positive operating cash flow.

Read: Taxes, accruals and earnings quality

Adverse selection

A contracting problem in which privately known characteristics influence who participates or which option they choose.

Distinguish hidden characteristics at contracting from hidden actions after contracting.

Read: Information, signaling and selection

Agency problem

A conflict between a person delegating a decision and the person taking it when their objectives or information differ.

An incentive payment must be evaluated together with participation, risk and feasible monitoring.

Read: Contracts, incentives and organizations

Arbitrage

A feasible trading strategy with no net investment that never loses and pays strictly positively in at least one relevant state, under the stated market convention.

Funding, short-sale, timing and transaction constraints belong to the definition of feasibility.

Read: Arbitrage, state prices and discount factors

Asset

A resource or contractual claim with future economic benefits, subject to its ownership, timing and accounting context.

An asset of one party may be another party’s liability.

Read: Stocks, flows and balance sheets

Asset pricing kernel

A stochastic discount factor that prices the traded payoffs by their expected discounted value under a stated probability law.

It need not be unique when the traded assets do not span all states.

Read: Arbitrage, state prices and discount factors

Bayes’ rule

An update from prior probabilities and a likelihood to conditional probabilities after observing evidence.

The conditioning event must have positive probability in the elementary event formula.

Read: Conditional probability and Bayes

Bellman equation

A recursive value equation equating optimal continuation value to the best current return plus discounted expected future value.

An equation’s solution needs a verification argument linking it to the infinite-horizon objective.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Bias of an estimator

The estimator’s repeated-sample expectation minus the parameter being estimated under a specified data-generating law.

An unbiased estimator can still be imprecise; low prediction error does not establish causal identification.

Read: Sampling and estimation

Budget constraint

The set of purchases, transfers and asset choices affordable with explicitly dated resources and permitted financing.

Write ownership and repayment obligations before optimizing.

Read: Preferences and consumer choice

Capital adequacy

The relationship between loss-absorbing capital and the exposures and requirements used in a specified prudential framework.

Book equity, regulatory capital and liquid assets are different quantities.

Read: Bank balance sheets, capital and liquidity

Capital asset pricing model

An equilibrium model relating expected excess return to covariance with the market portfolio under restrictive investment and market assumptions.

A sample regression slope alone does not validate those equilibrium assumptions.

Read: CAPM and equilibrium risk pricing

Cash flow

A receipt or payment over an interval, classified by the activity and accounting convention being used.

Do not add an end-of-period balance to a period’s cash flow without a reconciliation.

Read: Balance sheet, income statement and cash flow

Causal estimand

The precisely defined causal quantity a design aims to learn, including population, treatment, outcome, timing and comparison.

An estimator targets an estimand only under an identification argument.

Read: Identification, estimands and asymptotic tools

Collateral

An asset pledged to support an obligation under a specified enforcement and valuation arrangement.

Its market value, usable borrowing value and liquidation proceeds can differ.

Read: Credit analysis and lending decisions

Comparative advantage

A lower opportunity cost of producing one good relative to another.

Absolute productivity advantage in every good does not eliminate possible gains from specialization and exchange.

Read: Trade and comparative advantage

Comparative statics

A comparison of model solutions after changing a primitive while holding the other stated primitives fixed.

It is not automatically a prediction about a historical change involving many simultaneous shifts.

Read: Convexity, duality and comparative statics

Competitive equilibrium

Prices and allocations such that agents optimize over their feasible sets and all relevant markets clear with consistent ownership and budgets.

Feasibility alone does not establish individual optimality.

Read: General equilibrium and welfare

Complementary slackness

The condition that a nonnegative constraint multiplier times the associated slack is zero at a qualified optimum.

The condition must be combined with feasibility, stationarity and the relevant sufficiency assumptions.

Read: Unconstrained and constrained optimization

Compounding

Accumulation of a return on both the original amount and previously accumulated returns according to a specified timing convention.

An annual effective rate differs from a nominal rate compounded several times per year.

Read: Compounding and present value

Conditional expectation

A random variable measurable with respect to the conditioning information that preserves integrals over events in that information set.

Its value depends on the information available; nonlinear functions generally do not commute with expectation.

Read: Joint distributions and conditional expectation

Confidence interval

A random interval procedure with a stated repeated-sample coverage probability under its assumptions.

After observing the data, frequentist coverage is a property of the procedure, not a posterior probability for a fixed parameter.

Read: Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests

Confounding

A failure of a proposed causal comparison to isolate the treatment effect because treatment assignment and potential outcomes share determinants.

Including many controls does not itself supply an identification argument.

Read: Identification and confounding

Contraction

A map that shrinks distances by a common factor strictly below one on a stated metric space.

A fixed-point guarantee also requires the relevant completeness and mapping assumptions.

Read: Real analysis and convergence

Convexity

The property that every line segment joining two points in a set remains in the set; for functions, values along segments lie below the corresponding chord.

Convex feasible sets and concave maximands make local first-order conditions more informative about global optimality.

Read: Convexity, duality and comparative statics

Correlation

Covariance divided by the product of strictly positive standard deviations.

It is undefined when either variance is zero and does not by itself identify causation.

Read: Expectation, variance and covariance

Counterfactual

An outcome or allocation under a specified alternative intervention, action or model condition.

State which conditions are held fixed and how the alternative is defined.

Read: Models, causation and economic arguments

Covariance

The expectation of the product of two variables’ deviations from their means when the required moments exist.

Its units are the product of the variables’ units; its magnitude changes with rescaling.

Read: Expectation, variance and covariance

Credit spread

A yield or rate difference relative to a specified benchmark at matched conventions.

It can reflect default, liquidity, optionality and other components rather than pure expected default loss.

Read: Credit risk and recovery

Crowding out

A reduction in one activity induced by a change elsewhere through resource constraints, prices or incentives in a stated model.

Its size and even sign depend on the mechanism and economic conditions.

Read: Fiscal policy and public debt

Deferred acceptance

A proposal-and-rejection matching procedure with tentative holds, defined for stated preference and capacity rules.

Stability and incentive properties depend on the exact market domain and proposing side.

Read: Matching, networks and market design

Depreciation

A decline or allocation of capital’s value or productive capacity over time, as defined by the economic or accounting model.

Accounting depreciation expense is not a new cash payment in the period it is recorded.

Read: Long-lived assets and investment accounting

Difference-in-differences

A comparison of outcome changes across groups used to identify a treatment effect under a suitable untreated-trend restriction and other design assumptions.

Pre-treatment similarity alone cannot prove the required counterfactual trend.

Read: Difference-in-differences and event studies

Discount factor

A weight translating a dated payoff or utility into the valuation units of another date.

Preference discounting, deterministic market discounting and a stochastic pricing kernel are distinct objects.

Read: Compounding and present value

Diversification

Combining exposures so that imperfectly aligned payoffs reduce some aggregate risk relative to concentrated positions.

It need not eliminate common risk, illiquidity or losses caused by shared funding constraints.

Read: Portfolio mathematics and diversification

Dominance

A comparison under which one alternative is at least as good in every relevant state, distributional criterion or strategic contingency and strictly better in the required sense.

Always specify whether the criterion is payoff, first-order stochastic, second-order stochastic or strategic dominance.

Read: Uncertainty and information

Double-entry accounting

Recording each transaction with balancing debits and credits across accounts.

A balanced ledger can still contain a classification or measurement error.

Read: Transactions and double-entry accounting

Duration

A first-order measure of bond price sensitivity to a specified yield or curve movement, with several conventions.

A duration hedge can leave convexity, basis, credit and nonparallel curve risks.

Read: Duration, convexity and immunization

Economic profit

Revenue minus all relevant economic costs, including opportunity costs under the stated decision.

A positive accounting profit can coexist with a negative economic profit.

Read: Production, costs and firm choice

Elasticity

A dimensionless local percentage response of one variable to a percentage change in another where the relevant derivatives and levels permit it.

Its sign, conditioning set and point of evaluation matter.

Read: Derivatives and economic change

Endogeneity

Dependence between an explanatory variable and the disturbance in a specified estimating equation, or joint determination inside an economic model.

The two uses should be distinguished; an instrument requires more than correlation with the regressor.

Read: Instrumental variables and GMM

Equity

The residual ownership claim after the applicable obligations, with rights defined by the institution or contract.

Book equity and the market value of equity need not coincide.

Read: Equity, consolidation and ownership

Euler equation

An intertemporal first-order condition comparing a current marginal cost to expected discounted marginal benefit along feasible interior variations.

At a binding constraint an inequality may replace equality; even equality needs feasibility and terminal conditions.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Expected shortfall

A tail-loss measure obtained from the upper loss quantiles under an explicitly stated confidence convention.

Atoms require a quantile-based or appropriately fractional tail definition rather than naive conditioning on losses above VaR.

Read: Market risk and portfolio loss

Expected utility

The probability-weighted evaluation of outcomes through a utility index under a specified preference representation.

The probabilities, feasible lotteries and representation assumptions must be stated.

Read: Expected utility and risk preferences

Externality

An effect of one agent’s action on another that is not fully incorporated into the relevant private decision prices or contracts.

A corrective instrument must account for the marginal social effect and its implementation constraints.

Read: Externalities and public goods

Factor model

A representation relating asset returns to common factors, exposures and residual components.

A statistical factor representation is not by itself a causal or equilibrium pricing explanation.

Read: Factor models and empirical asset pricing

Feasibility

Satisfaction of the model’s resource, technology, information and contractual constraints.

A feasible allocation need not be optimal, incentive compatible or an equilibrium.

Read: Theory synthesis and research critique

Fixed effect

A unit- or period-specific intercept used to absorb a stated class of additive unobserved components.

Removing fixed additive components does not remove all time-varying confounding.

Read: Panel data and longitudinal identification

Forward contract

An agreement to exchange a specified underlying asset or cash equivalent at a future date on agreed terms.

A quoted forward price is distinct from the contract’s current value.

Read: Forwards, futures and swaps

Free cash flow

Cash available to a specified class of capital providers after the operating and investment uses in the adopted definition.

Match firm cash flow with enterprise-value discounting and equity cash flow with equity discounting.

Read: Free cash flow and discounting

Generalized method of moments

Estimation using population moment restrictions and a stated sample weighting criterion.

Identification, instrument validity and uncertainty treatment are separate from numerical minimization.

Read: Instrumental variables and GMM

Gross domestic product

A measure of production within a defined economic territory over an interval under national-accounting conventions.

It is a flow and is not a balance sheet, wealth total or complete welfare measure.

Read: National accounts and macro measurement

Hedging

Choosing offsetting exposures to reduce a specified risk under stated market and model conditions.

A hedge can introduce basis, liquidity, execution or model risk.

Read: Greeks, volatility and hedging

Identification

Uniqueness or partial restriction of a target across data-generating structures consistent with the observable evidence and maintained assumptions.

More observations reduce sampling uncertainty without necessarily resolving observational equivalence.

Read: Identification, estimands and asymptotic tools

Immunization

Construction of a portfolio intended to meet liability-value or sensitivity conditions under specified interest-rate movements.

Matching a few sensitivities does not guarantee funding under every curve or spread change.

Read: Duration, convexity and immunization

Incentive compatibility

A restriction that each agent prefers the prescribed action or truthful report to all deviations allowed by the mechanism and information structure.

Check the full deviation set, not only a selected neighboring deviation unless a theorem justifies that reduction.

Read: Information economics and screening

Instrumental variable

A variable used to identify an endogenous effect through relevance and substantive exogeneity or exclusion conditions in a stated model.

First-stage strength does not establish exclusion.

Read: Instrumental variables and GMM

Internal rate of return

A discount rate at which a specified stream of net cash flows has zero net present value.

A stream may have multiple such rates or none; project ranking still requires consistent valuation assumptions.

Read: Value creation and capital budgeting

Inverse probability weighting

Reweighting observations using treatment, selection or sampling probabilities to target a stated population quantity under design assumptions.

Positivity and the accuracy or known design status of the probabilities matter.

Read: Experiments and causal inference

Ito correction

The second-derivative term generated by the quadratic variation of a diffusion when applying Ito’s formula.

Ordinary deterministic chain rules omit this stochastic term.

Read: Brownian motion and Ito calculus

KKT conditions

Karush–Kuhn–Tucker feasibility, multiplier, stationarity and complementary-slackness conditions for constrained optimization under appropriate regularity.

Necessity and sufficiency have different hypotheses; do not infer a global optimum solely from stationarity.

Read: Unconstrained and constrained optimization

Leverage

Exposure or asset holdings relative to an explicitly named equity, capital or funding base.

Different denominators produce different leverage measures, and leverage amplifies losses as well as gains.

Read: Bank balance sheets, capital and liquidity

Likelihood

The probability mass or density of the observed data treated as a function of model parameters.

It is not a probability distribution over the parameters unless combined with a prior and normalized as a posterior.

Read: Likelihood and nonlinear models

Liquidity

The ability to trade an asset or obtain funding on acceptable terms within the relevant time horizon.

Market liquidity and funding liquidity interact but are distinct.

Read: Liquidity, funding and asset-liability management

Marginal decision

A choice based on the incremental benefit and incremental cost of a feasible change.

An equality rule may fail at a boundary, at a discrete choice or without global concavity.

Read: Incentives, marginal decisions and equilibrium

Market completeness

The ability of traded claims to span every relevant state-contingent payoff in the specified finite-state benchmark.

No-arbitrage can hold without completeness and then need not select a unique price for an untraded claim.

Read: Incomplete markets and advanced derivatives

Markov state

A state that contains the information needed for the conditional law of future evolution given current decisions.

A convenient variable is not automatically a sufficient state.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Matching stability

The absence of a blocking deviation under the matching model’s specified agents, preferences and permitted coalitions.

Pairwise stability, group stability and efficiency are different properties.

Read: Matching, networks and market design

Mean reversion

A conditional tendency to move toward a long-run reference level under a stated stochastic law.

It is not a promise that a realized path will quickly return to its mean.

Read: Time series, forecasting and financial econometrics

Moral hazard

An incentive problem involving an action that cannot be fully observed or contracted upon by another party.

Risk sharing and incentive provision must be considered together.

Read: Contracts, incentives and organizations

Nash equilibrium

A profile of strategies in which no player can improve their payoff by an allowed unilateral deviation given the others’ strategies.

It need not be efficient, unique, dynamically stable or robust to a changed information structure.

Read: Static games and refinements

Net present value

The value of a consistently dated stream of net cash flows after discounting at rates appropriate to the cash-flow and risk assumptions.

A positive value depends on the forecast, financing convention and opportunity cost used.

Read: Value creation and capital budgeting

No-Ponzi restriction

A terminal borrowing restriction excluding financing plans that indefinitely roll over obligations without adequate backing under the stated valuation.

It should not be silently equated with every transversality condition.

Read: New Keynesian models and monetary policy · Fiscal policy and sovereign debt · Consumption, saving and investment

Opportunity cost

The value of the best feasible alternative forgone by a choice.

Sunk expenditure is not a recoverable alternative merely because it was paid in the past.

Read: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost

Option

A contractual right, with stated exercise terms, to choose a transaction or payoff without the corresponding exercise obligation.

The holder’s option value and the writer’s obligations depend on exercise, settlement and collateral terms.

Read: Options and binomial replication

Ordinary least squares

The coefficient choice minimizing the sum of squared residuals in a specified linear sample model.

Projection arithmetic alone does not establish causal interpretation or valid conventional standard errors.

Read: Regression as projection

Pareto efficiency

An allocation for which no feasible alternative makes someone better off without making anyone worse off.

It is not a distributional fairness criterion and depends on the feasible set and preferences.

Read: Welfare, aggregation and social choice

Policy iteration

An algorithm alternating evaluation of a fixed policy with policy improvement in a stated dynamic control problem.

Tie handling and the evaluation accuracy matter for its implementation and guarantee.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Posterior distribution

The conditional distribution of unknown quantities after updating a prior with a stated likelihood and observed evidence.

Posterior conclusions inherit the model, prior and measurement assumptions.

Read: Bayesian inference and decisions

Present value

The value assigned at a reference date to future or past dated amounts using a specified discounting rule.

Keep currencies, price levels, dates and risk treatment consistent.

Read: Compounding and present value

Price discrimination

Different effective pricing across buyers or purchase options that cannot be explained solely by matching cost differences under the stated definition.

Arbitrage, self-selection and participation restrict feasible pricing schemes.

Read: Monopoly, oligopoly and pricing

Principal–agent contract

A mechanism connecting transfers or decision rights to observable outcomes or reports when interests or information differ.

A contract optimum must respect participation, incentive and resource constraints.

Read: Contracts and dynamic incentives

Projection

The closest element of a specified subspace under an adopted inner product or norm.

An orthogonal projection describes approximation geometry, not necessarily an economic mechanism.

Read: Eigenvalues, projections and quadratic forms

Public good

A good characterized in the stated setting by nonrival use and difficulty of excluding users.

The financing and provision mechanism determines how preferences translate into supply.

Read: Externalities and public goods

Real exchange rate

A relative price of national consumption baskets or goods after currency conversion under an explicitly declared quotation convention.

An increase can mean depreciation or appreciation depending on the definition.

Read: Exchange rates and external balances

Real option

A valuable opportunity to adapt a physical or strategic investment decision after information arrives.

Option-like flexibility must be feasible and include exercise, delay and competition costs.

Read: Real options and investment timing

Regression discontinuity

A design using treatment assignment changes at a cutoff to identify a local effect under continuity or an appropriate local-randomization argument.

Manipulation, other cutoff changes and bandwidth choices can undermine the comparison.

Read: Regression discontinuity and synthetic controls

Replication

An attempt to reconstruct or reassess a reported result using specified data, code or a new sample, with the exact aim stated.

Numerical reproduction with original inputs and independent replication of a finding are different claims.

Read: Empirical integration and replication

Revelation principle

A result translating a specified equilibrium outcome into a truthful direct mechanism under maintained feasibility and information assumptions.

It does not remove participation, budget balance, commitment or equilibrium-selection requirements.

Read: Mechanism design and auctions

Risk premium

Compensation measured relative to a specified safe return or certainty-equivalent benchmark for bearing risk.

An expected-return premium differs from a utility-based monetary risk premium.

Read: Expected utility and risk preferences

Risk-neutral probability

A pricing probability under which appropriately discounted traded values satisfy the required martingale relation in the model.

It need not equal the physical probability of events.

Read: Black-Scholes and risk-neutral valuation

Selection bias

A distortion relative to a target caused by a selection process that the analysis does not adequately account for.

Define the target population and selection mechanism before deciding whether a difference is bias.

Read: Identification and confounding

Shadow price

The marginal value of relaxing a resource or constraint under the sign, units and regularity of a stated optimization problem.

A multiplier need not be a market price, and a derivative interpretation requires justification.

Read: Convexity, duality and comparative statics

Sharpe ratio

Expected excess return divided by return standard deviation over a specified period when the denominator is positive.

Comparison requires consistent periods and return conventions; it does not summarize all tail or liquidity risk.

Read: Active management and performance evaluation

Signaling

An informed party’s action that affects another party’s beliefs and subsequent choices.

The information conveyed depends on equilibrium incentives and off-path beliefs.

Read: Information economics and screening

Solvency

The ability to satisfy obligations according to a stated valuation, horizon and admissible adjustment set.

A solvent institution can still face a liquidity shortfall before its assets pay off.

Read: Liquidity, funding and asset-liability management

State price

The current price of a claim paying one unit in a particular future state and zero in the other states in a specified complete-payoff representation.

State prices combine time and risk valuation and are not generally probabilities.

Read: Arbitrage, state prices and discount factors

Stationarity

Invariance of a specified distributional feature under time shifts; strict and covariance stationarity impose different requirements.

It does not by itself imply independence, ergodicity or constant realized observations.

Read: Time series, forecasting and financial econometrics

Stochastic dominance

A ranking of distributions that implies a utility comparison over a specified class of utility functions.

The order and integrability/domain conditions determine which preference comparisons follow.

Read: Uncertainty and information

Stock and flow

A stock is measured at a date; a flow is measured over an interval and can change a stock through an accounting law.

Balances require beginning stock plus net flows and any valuation or other adjustments.

Read: Stocks, flows and balance sheets

Stress test

An assessment of losses, funding or other outcomes under explicitly chosen adverse scenarios and behavioral assumptions.

A severe scenario is not automatically a probability-calibrated quantile or a forecast.

Read: Stress testing and risk aggregation

Subgame perfection

A strategy profile that is a Nash equilibrium in every subgame of an extensive-form game.

Information sets determine which continuation portions are subgames.

Read: Dynamic and repeated games

Sufficient statistic

A statistic retaining all sample information about a parameter in the precise factorization or conditional-distribution sense of a stated statistical model.

It is a model-relative claim, not a general declaration that other data are economically irrelevant. The contract chapter supplies a finite action-family illustration; the econometrics chapter supplies likelihood background.

Read: Contracts and dynamic incentives · Likelihood and nonlinear models

Sunk cost

A cost already incurred that cannot be changed or recovered by the current alternatives.

It affects wealth but should not be counted as a new avoidable cost when comparing current actions.

Read: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost

Synthetic control

A constructed comparison using weighted donor outcomes to approximate an untreated trajectory under a specified design.

Fit before treatment does not alone identify the counterfactual after treatment.

Read: Regression discontinuity and synthetic controls

Terminal value

The value at a forecast boundary assigned to subsequent cash flows or remaining assets under a stated continuation model.

It must be dated and financed consistently with the forecast’s investment and growth assumptions.

Read: Valuation models and terminal assumptions

Transversality condition

A limiting condition involving the value of terminal states or assets used in an optimality argument for an infinite-horizon problem.

Its necessity or sufficiency depends on the domain and proof; Euler equalities alone are generally insufficient.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Treatment effect

A contrast of outcomes under defined treatment alternatives for a unit or target population.

Average, local, conditional and distributional effects answer different questions.

Read: Experiments and causal inference

Value at risk

A specified loss quantile at a stated confidence level and horizon.

It does not report the size of losses beyond that quantile.

Read: Market risk and portfolio loss

Value iteration

Repeated application of a Bellman operator to approximate its fixed point under appropriate assumptions.

A residual bound needs a valid operator norm and contraction constant for the stated problem.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Variance

The expected squared deviation from the mean when finite.

It has squared units and is not a complete description of a distribution’s tails.

Read: Expectation, variance and covariance

WACC

A weighted average cost of capital under stated market-value weights, financing, tax and risk assumptions.

It cannot be applied indiscriminately to cash flows with changing risk or inconsistent financing treatment.

Read: Risk, cost of capital and WACC

Welfare weight

A coefficient describing how an explicit social objective values an individual’s or group’s welfare change.

It is a normative input requiring justification, not a fact inferred from an accounting identity.

Read: Welfare, aggregation and social choice

Working capital

A specified set of operating current assets net of operating current liabilities, with its scope declared.

Different conventions include or exclude cash and debt; valuation must use the same definition throughout.

Read: Revenue, working capital and operating cycles

Yield to maturity

The single discount rate equating a bond’s quoted price convention to its promised dated cash flows.

It is not automatically the realized return when there is default, early sale or reinvestment at other rates.

Read: Bond cash flows and yield curves

Notation and units

Before calculating, write the date, currency or physical unit, price basis, probability law and information set. For a rate, state the interval and whether it is a gross return, net rate, continuous intensity or per-period probability. Read a prime, hat or bar from the chapter’s definition rather than assuming a universal meaning.

t, t+1

Current and next dates; the interval length is specified locally.

Never combine annual and monthly rates without conversion.

Read: Compounding and present value · Stochastic growth and real business cycles

Δx, dx

A finite change and a differential, respectively.

A derivative approximation is not an exact finite change.

Read: Derivatives and economic change

%, pp

Percent and percentage points.

Moving from 2% to 3% is 1 percentage point and a 50% relative increase.

Read: Numbers, units and percentage changes

E[X], E[X | I]

Expectation and expectation conditional on information I.

State the probability law, information and existence of the relevant moments.

Read: Joint distributions and conditional expectation

P, p

A probability law, transition matrix, price or parameter, depending on the chapter.

Read the local definition: a price vector is not a transition matrix.

Read: Probability spaces and counting · Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

Var(X), Cov(X,Y), Corr(X,Y)

Variance, covariance and correlation.

Correlation requires nonzero standard deviations; covariance carries product units.

Read: Expectation, variance and covariance

β

A preference discount factor, regression coefficient or CAPM exposure in different models.

The same glyph does not impose the same restrictions across chapters.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods · Linear models and robust inference · CAPM and equilibrium risk pricing

α

A capital exponent, test significance level, intercept or abnormal-return measure in different contexts.

Its units and permitted range follow the local model.

Read: Stochastic growth and real business cycles · Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests · Active management and performance evaluation

δ

A depreciation rate, discount-related parameter or other locally defined coefficient.

Continuous-time rates and per-period fractions are not interchangeable.

Read: Growth and the Solow model

σ, σ², Σ

A standard deviation, variance or covariance matrix under the usual local conventions.

A strategy or another object can also use σ in game theory.

Read: Expectation, variance and covariance · Portfolio mathematics and diversification · Static games and refinements

μ

A mean, drift, probability distribution or constraint multiplier.

Dimensions and indexing determine which interpretation applies.

Read: Brownian motion and Ito calculus · Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

λ

A constraint multiplier, intensity or eigenvalue.

Multiplier signs depend on how the constraint enters the Lagrangian.

Read: Unconstrained and constrained optimization · Eigenvalues, projections and quadratic forms

r, R

Often a net rate r and gross return R = 1 + r, but also rental rates or cash payoffs locally.

Check whether depreciation is included in a capital return.

Read: Returns, payoffs and investment opportunity sets · Stochastic growth and real business cycles

i, π

Often a nominal interest rate and inflation; i also indexes agents and π can mean profit or a probability vector.

The exact gross Fisher relation is multiplicative when used as an ex-post return identity.

Read: Prices, inflation and purchasing power · Static games and refinements

q

A quantity, bond price, Tobin-type valuation ratio or probability.

Its denominator and units must be identified before interpretation.

Read: Bond cash flows and yield curves · Arbitrage, state prices and discount factors

w, W

A wage or portfolio weight vector, and sometimes wealth or a value function.

A wage is priced per unit of labor; a portfolio weight requires a defined capital base.

Read: Stochastic growth and real business cycles · Portfolio mathematics and diversification

k, K

Individual or aggregate capital in growth models, or a strike price in options.

Capital timing differs from a contract’s fixed strike.

Read: Stochastic growth and real business cycles · Options and binomial replication

c, C

Consumption, a cost function or an option value depending on context.

Preserve whether the object is a flow, discounted value or function.

Read: Production, costs and firm choice · Black-Scholes and risk-neutral valuation · Stochastic growth and real business cycles

a, A

Assets, an action, a matrix or productivity, with case and indexing carrying meaning.

Individual assets and aggregate states differ in a household’s price-taking problem.

Read: Vectors, matrices and linear systems · Stochastic growth and real business cycles

u, U

A utility function, unemployment rate or continuation value.

A utility index is not a monetary quantity without a specified conversion.

Read: Expected utility and risk preferences · Labor markets and unemployment

V

A value function or current valuation, as locally defined.

A Bellman value can be unbounded even when its value differences or special coefficient system are tractable.

Read: Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

m, M

A stochastic discount factor, matching function or matrix.

In asset pricing p = E[mX] requires compatible payoff and currency units.

Read: Arbitrage, state prices and discount factors · Labor markets and unemployment

x̂

A log deviation, estimate or approximation, depending on the declared convention.

A log deviation log(x/x̄) requires strictly positive levels; it is not always (x−x̄)/x̄ exactly.

Read: Stochastic growth and real business cycles · Sampling and estimation

x̄

A mean, steady-state level or bound.

A steady-state value is not necessarily a sample mean.

Read: Growth and the Solow model · Sampling and estimation

x*

An optimizer, equilibrium candidate or other selected benchmark.

The star labels a claim or definition; the supporting proof establishes optimality.

Read: Unconstrained and constrained optimization

x′, Aᵀ

A next-period choice or derivative for x′; matrix transpose for Aᵀ.

The chapter must disambiguate a prime used for time from a prime used for differentiation.

Read: Derivatives and economic change · Vectors, matrices and linear systems · Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

∇f, Hf

Gradient and Hessian of a differentiable scalar function.

The order and units of coordinates matter in quadratic approximations.

Read: Multivariable calculus

‖x‖, ‖x‖∞

A stated norm and the maximum absolute coordinate norm in finite dimensions.

A numerical error certificate must use the same norm as its theorem.

Read: Numerical methods and dynamic foundations · Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

≈, =

Approximate equality and exact equality.

State the approximation order, numerical tolerance or rounding convention.

Read: Computational reliability and numerical audits

⇒, ⇔

Logical implication and equivalence.

A necessary condition gives one direction; sufficiency gives the other.

Read: Mathematical language and proof

argmax, max, sup

The maximizing choices, attained largest value and least upper bound.

The supremum can exist without any maximizing choice.

Read: Unconstrained and constrained optimization · Dynamic optimization and recursive methods

a.s., in probability, in distribution

Different modes of convergence or probability-one qualification.

They have distinct definitions and cannot be substituted without a theorem.

Read: Large samples and convergence · Measure and stochastic foundations

O(h²), o(h)

A quantity bounded by a constant times h² near the limit, and a quantity whose ratio to h tends to zero.

A local order statement does not give a global numerical error bound.

Read: Numerical methods and dynamic foundations

basis point

One hundredth of a percentage point.

100 basis points equals 1 percentage point, not necessarily a 1% relative change.

Read: Numbers, units and percentage changes · Duration, convexity and immunization

log x

Natural logarithm unless another base is explicitly given.

Its argument must be positive and consistently scaled; log changes differ from simple changes.

Read: Returns, payoffs and investment opportunity sets · Stochastic growth and real business cycles

PV, NPV, FV

Present value, net present value and future value.

Every amount requires a valuation date, currency and consistent cash-flow treatment.

Read: Compounding and present value · Value creation and capital budgeting

CE, EV, CV

Certainty equivalent, equivalent variation and compensating variation.

Certainty equivalents depend on preferences; money-metric welfare measures specify their price reference.

Read: Expected utility and risk preferences · Demand, duality and welfare

ATE, ATT, LATE

Average treatment effect, average effect on treated units and a local average treatment effect under its instrumental-variable interpretation.

The target population and identifying assumptions differ.

Read: Experiments and causal inference · Instrumental variables and GMM

VaR, ES

Value at risk and expected shortfall for a stated loss variable, confidence and horizon.

Specify loss sign, quantile convention and atom treatment.

Read: Market risk and portfolio loss

GDP, GNI

Gross domestic product and gross national income.

Production territory and income accruing to residents are different accounting concepts.

Read: National accounts and macro measurement
